summary: This diff fixes a real bug in construction-boq-import-service.ts's header-to-field mapping: mapBoqHeaders previously picked the first header (in sheet order) matching any alias for a field, which meant a spreadsheet with both a 'Category' and a 'Description (Task)' column could have 'category' win the description slot purely by column position; the fix makes alias matching try each field's aliases in priority order across all headers, so a dedicated description column always beats the 'category' fallback, plus adds 'sl no' as a recognized itemCode alias and a new subTask field with positional parent-child inference for unlabeled sub-task rows (Frame/Gypsum Board/etc.) that carry a Breakdown % but no itemCode of their own. I traced the mapBoqHeaders and mapRowsToLineItems logic by hand against the new xlsx-based regression test's exact row shapes (category header rows, multi-line descriptions with embedded 'Location :' text, unlabeled sub-task rows) and confirmed the mapping and parent-attachment results match the test's assertions, including that positional inference correctly resets at each new parent task row so sub-tasks never bleed across tasks. The change is scoped entirely to the import/parsing layer (computeHierarchicalAmount untouched, matching the stated constraint), the only other reference to this module (src/app/api/construction/boq/import/route.ts) calls parseBoqSpreadsheet and already uses requireAuth(), and is unaffected by the alias-priority change. No auth, schema, migration, payment, billing, RLS, or .github/workflows/** paths are touched, and the diff is additive (91 insertions to the service file plus a new test block) rather than a heavy deletion, so tier1 is the correct classification.
